message.content: {"B_expression":"-1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))**2)","C_expression":"-1/(sqrt(1+r)*(1+sqrt(1+r)))","derivation":"Retained unchanged from P04_W1 (generation 1). The local algebra is: with g = r/2 + chi_r*chi_u*(r^2*B + u*r*C), setting chi_r=chi_u=1 and requiring the pure quadratic remainder 2g+g^2-r to vanish gives B = -1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))^2), yielding g0 = sqrt(1+r)-1. The C-term is obtained by setting the O(u) coefficient of the full residual E = (2g+g^2-r) + 2*u*g to zero: with g = g0 + u*r*C, the O(u) part is 2*r*C*(1+g0) + 2*g0, which vanishes when C = -g0/(r*(1+g0)) = -1/(sqrt(1+r)*(1+sqrt(1+r))). The residual then reduces to O(u^2) + O(r^2) inside the chi support. Both bodies are C-infinity for r > -1, strictly containing the outer rectangle r in [-1/2, 1/2]. Numerical confirmation at generation 1 (all rows in the feedback): in-support UNIFORM points show pure ~ O(r^2) ~ 1e-8 to 1e-6 and cross ~ O(u*r) ~ 1e-8 to 1e-6, with their sum (the total residual) at ~1e-11, confirming the near-cancellation. Out-of-support points (|r|>1/4 or |u|>1/4) correctly receive g=r/2 with no correction. ZERO rows remain exactly 1.0. No revision is warranted by the observed data.","inspect":[],"note":"Program retained at generation 2, identical to generations 0 and 1. The in-support residuals are at the expected O(r^2)+O(u^2) floor. A successor should verify at the next stage (t=1/256 or t=1/128 with accumulated u from prior corrections) that points with moderate |u| (e.g., 0.007 to 0.03) still show the O(u^2) residual structure, and that the chi transition boundaries (|r|=1/4, |u|=1/8 for full support; |r|=1/2, |u|=1/4 for outer edge) are handled smoothly by the C-infinity step functions. Points far outside support (|u|>1/4 or |r|>1/2) will continue to use g=r/2 with no correction, which is by design and not a failure. The analytic certificate remains ANALYTIC_ON_CORE_NEIGHBORHOOD for both bodies; the composite with the chi transitions is smooth but the formal all-order certificate is NOT_CERTIFIED, which does not affect the numerical answer."}
